title: Structured output contract and regression harness for JSON-mode & constrained decoding
creator: Marcel Tan
description:
Objective: Build a deterministic test harness and contract suite that validates structured output behavior end-to-end across streaming, function/tool calling, and compatibility layers. This ticket covers: 1) JSON-mode enforcement tests that exercise both non-streaming and streaming codepaths, 2) constrained-decoding regression tests that verify the decoder limits token outputs to a validated schema, and 3) compatibility checks that map legacy SDK params (eg. json_mode=true) to the new structured_output contract.

Scope: create a suite that runs in CI, produces clear failure reasons, includes fuzzed malformed outputs, and provides mitigation recommendations (postprocessing heuristics) when models deviate from schema. Tests must run against: hosted API stubs, dedicated environment (small GPU fleet), and a local private runtime image to catch environment-specific regressions.

Why: We keep seeing production incidents where streaming chunks or partial function-call payloads break downstream parsers. Constrained decoding reduces these incidents but has subtle failure modes (truncated JSON, stray tokens). We need reproducible failures and an automated contract that prevents regressions during model upgrades, runtime changes, and SDK compatibility shims.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs a structured-output test job on every runtime change and fail fast on schema violations
Streaming chunk validator can reassemble partial chunks and assert schema at both chunk and final payload levels
Constrained-decoding test vectors cover edge cases: unterminated arrays, extra trailing tokens, nested object depth limits, and escaped characters
Compatibility shim unit tests cover mapping from legacy params (json_mode=true) to new structured_output API surface across SDKs
Regression harness produces a minimal reproducible prompt+seed for any failing case and uploads artifacts to the test run (logs, raw tokens, reassembly trace)
tasks: Design test plan and golden schemas for 4 canonical contracts: simple object, nested object, list-of-objects, function-call payload
Implement streaming chunk validator that verifies both incremental validity (no invalid token sequences) and final schema adherence
Add constrained-decoding fuzz harness that injects token-level anomalies and asserts the runtime's rejection or safe fallback
Create SDK compatibility tests that translate old param variants into the structured_output contract and assert identical behavior
Wire the harness into CI with thresholded flaky-tolerance and automatic artifact storage for failures
Write docs for engineers: how to write new structured-output tests and add new schema contracts
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff sync with Runtime and SDK teams. Agreed on 4 canonical schema shapes and a single canonical JSON Schema draft stored in Drive.
2025-02-13: PoC streaming validator implemented (nodejs) that reassembles chunks and runs Ajv against final payload; early flakiness observed when using small max_chunk_size.
2025-02-16: Added token-level tracing to PoC to capture raw token ids and tokenization boundaries for malformed outputs; captured 3 unique failure modes from deduped synthetic runs.

2025-02-20: First CI job integrated on staging runners. Two failing cases: (1) function-call name appears partial across two chunks and (2) escaped newline inside string produced unbalanced quotes for ajv. Creating targeted constrained-decoding vectors.
2025-02-22: Implemented compatibility shim tests mapping legacy json_mode param to structured_output v1; SDK team reviewed and requested one additional mapping for streaming flags.
decisions: Use Ajv (JSON Schema) as the canonical validator for contract tests rather than custom parsers to reduce false positives
Validator will run at two phases: chunk-level sanity checks (no control chars that break tokenizers) and final-schema checks on reassembled payload

When schema fails in streaming, harness will attempt two deterministic repair strategies: smart-concat (concatenate last N chunks) and bracket-salvage (attempt to close open braces); both must be logged and flagged as non-authoritative
Compatibility layer will normalize legacy params into structured_output object server-side to minimize SDK patchwork; SDK tests will assert parity only, not server translation logic
notes: Edge case: streaming with partial UTF-8 codepoints that split across chunks should be normalized by runtime before validator runs
Tool-calling interaction: function-call payloads must include 'name' and 'arguments' keys; validator will assert argument types and length limits to avoid downstream crash
We will add a small corpus of adversarial prompts (50) that historically caused broken JSON outputs; include model seeds to reproduce nondeterministic behaviors
blocking_issues: Need deterministic small-scale dedicated fleet to run fuzzing (ops ticket: INF-ops-63)
Runtime must expose token-level trace hooks for CI; currently behind feature flag
